resume: Free offers at 15 and 16, €50 at 17, €150 at 18: the documents to prepare for registering in the app and the time limits for using it.
aQuoiCaSert: The pass Culture (France's culture pass for young people) makes culture easier to access: books, cinema tickets, concerts, shows, lessons, musical instruments. It has an individual part, used by the young person in the app, and a collective part, used by teachers for class outings. Bookings are made in the app, with partner venues.
quiEstConcerne: Young people aged 15 to 18 living in mainland France or in an overseas département, whether in school or not.
Young foreign nationals who have lived in France for at least 1 year.
aSavoir: Young people registered since March 1, 2025: free offers at 15 and 16, €50 at 17, €150 at 18. The credits at 17 and 18 add up.
The money can be used until the day before the young person turns 21.

Since an order published in the Journal officiel (France's official gazette) on December 30, 2025, online offers (music, video, video games, audiobooks, digital press) are capped at €50 in total, except for young people with a recognized disability.

A €50 bonus after 18 is planned for young people with a disability (AEEH, disabled child education allowance; AAH, adult disability allowance) or whose household's family quotient is below a threshold set each year.

Registration: ID and proof of address in the young person's name. If they live with someone else, you also need that person's proof of address, a letter confirming they house the young person (attestation d'hébergement) and that person's ID. Students can also create their account through ÉduConnect (the schools' login service), with a code provided by their school.
